title: Launch cadence telemetry and rollback decision tree
creator: Claire Robertson
description: Objective: create a repeatable playbook that ties launch calendar signals (capacity, canary results, latency spikes, regression alerts) into a telemetry-backed decision tree for go/no-go and automated soft rollback triggers. This ticket will define signal thresholds, required dashboards/alerts, owner handoffs, and the decision-tree that Release Managers and on-call SREs use during multi-surface launches (runtime, console, API). Deliverables: telemetry spec, Grafana dashboard, decision-tree doc, small automation for auto-fallback to variant models or capacity lanes, and runbook steps for manual rollback escalation.
updates: 2026-02-20 - Created ticket and drafted high-level goals; initial review with Release Managers scheduled.
2026-02-25 - Scoped signals: latency p95, token cost delta, error-rate, model-quality regression via evals; asked ENG to validate metric availability (ENG-4829).
2026-03-02 - Design sync: agreed on three-tier decisions (green / watch / revert) and fallback lanes (model-variant, lower-capacity tier, region failover).

2026-03-08 - PoC dashboard created in staging Grafana; linked to canary cluster metrics and eval-set quality hooks. Feedback: make thresholds percentile-relative and include recent quantization rollouts.
2026-03-12 - Draft decision tree documented; next: automation spike for soft-fallback (ENG PR) and runbook playtest with staging cutover rehearsal (2026-03-22).
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry spec approved by Runtime, Console, and API leads
Grafana dashboard with key panels (latency p50/p95/p99, error-rate, cost-per-token delta, eval-quality signal) deployed to staging and prod
Decision tree published in Confluence with owner and SLA per branch
Automation prototype that performs soft-fallback to pre-defined model variant or lower-capacity lane during 'revert' branch merged to ops repo
Runbook validated in a dry-run rehearsal with at least two Release Managers and one SRE
milestones: 2026-03-29 - Automation spike merged to ops and smoke-tested
risks: Important signals (eval quality during canary) may have >30s lag if downstream hooks are not optimized
Overly aggressive auto-fallback could cause churn; need guardrails and cooldown windows
Discrepancy between staging and prod signal distributions may cause false positives
Ownership gaps across runtime/console/api during multi-surface launches could delay decisions
communication_plan: Weekly sync with Runtime/Console/API leads, daily standups during rehearsal week, and a single Slack launch-channel (#launch-cadence) for real-time signals. Publish decision-tree summary to leadership 24h before a major release window.
rollout_strategy: Start with internal-only launches (shadow traffic + canary fraction 1%) for two release cycles, then expand to low-risk customer cohorts. Enable automated soft-fallback only in a 'watch' window for first two weeks before promoting to auto-trigger in critical windows.
qa_plan: Create synthetic traffic jobs that simulate token distribution, heavy KV-cache hits, and known failure modes. Validate that dashboard alerts fire and that the automation correctly transitions to fallback lanes without full rollback. Include one on-call SRE during tests.
observability_requirements: Eval-quality hook with pass/fail for regression test-set
Automated annotation of deployment metadata on metrics (rollout_id, canary_fraction, model_variant)
budget_considerations: Small ops budget for automation spike and extra Grafana retention during rehearsal (estimated $6k). If automation expands to cross-region failover, additional infra budget will be required—escalate to finance if >$20k.
notes: Decision: use percentile-relative thresholds (e.g., >2x baseline p95) rather than static ms thresholds to handle model size variance.
Trade-off: initial automation will prefer model-variant fallback over immediate rollback to minimize user-visible regressions.
Follow-up: create a template for future release trains so teams can plug in their project IDs and get a pre-populated dashboard and decision tree
